# int.parse is #[intrinsic("int.parse")]: every backend must have
# an emitter for it. Before these existed the Go path emitted a call to a
# function that did not exist and nothing caught it, because no test compiled
# the result — so the go case here builds rather than greps.
#
# It also pins that a placeholder body is dropped after type checking: while
# int.parse's `return 0` survived, the const folder answered 0 and no call was
# emitted at all.

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=outjs app.sngl
grep 'parseInt\("FF", 16\)' outjs/index.html

sngl generate --lang=kotlin --platform=android --opt=main=true --out=outkt app.sngl
grep 'toIntOrNull\(16\)' outkt/app/src/main/java/test/sngl/app/MainScreen.kt

[!exec:go] skip 'go toolchain required'
sngl build --lang=go --platform=bubbletea --opt name=np bt.sngl
exists np

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main node {
    var hex = int.parse("FF", 16)
    text(value=string(hex))
}

window {
    main
}
-- bt.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component main node {
    var hex = int.parse("FF", 16)
    text(value=string(hex))
}

window {
    main
}
